   - `risk_of_bias_tool`: Pick the single design-matched tool per `RISK_OF_BIAS.md` §1:
     * `"RoB 2 (parallel-trial variant)"` (individually randomized trial)
     * `"RoB 2 (cluster-randomized trials variant)"` (cluster-randomized trial — check unit of randomization carefully!)
     * `"ROBINS-I"` (non-randomized intervention / quasi-experimental study with a genuine comparator: DiD, IV, RDD, PSM, ITS, controlled before-after, policy panel FE)
     * `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies"` (quantitative cross-sectional survey / observational regression without quasi-experimental intervention comparator)

     * `"Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework"` (legal-empirical, doctrinal-empirical, jurimetric, or institutional-historical study that fits none of the six conventional designs above)
     * `"NONE"` (fits none of the listed tools, e.g., pure mathematical/simulation optimization model, or non-systematic narrative review/essay without primary empirical data or systematic search — explain why in `comment`)

(`"2"` = mechanism directly observed empirically; `"1"` = documented statistical/descriptive association; `"0"` = inferred only by authors).

country.comment: The study analyzes 20 municipalities with headquarters in the Eastern Watersheds (Bacias Hidrográficas do Leste, BHL) in the State of Bahia, Brazil.
country.where_found: PDF p. 2, Title/Affiliations; PDF p. 4, Section 1; PDF p. 5–6, Section 1

effect_estimate.comment: Descriptive quantitative and governance indicators only; no inferential statistical model, 95% confidence intervals, or p-values are reported. Note minor internal discrepancies in the paper: Table 1 lists 12 municipalities (with 'Uma' for Una) while text on PDF p. 20 states 13; Table 3 lists 4 non-responding municipalities while text on PDF p. 26 states 5.
effect_estimate.value: Descriptive analysis only (no regression point estimates, 95% CIs, or p-values reported). Across the 20 municipalities headquartered in Bahia's Bacias Hidrográficas do Leste (635,546 residents in 2017), 2017 sewage collection averaged 37.95% across 13 analyzed municipalities (vs. 54.65% Bahia state average; 4 municipalities had 0% collection), sewage treatment averaged 11.54% across 17 municipalities (vs. 50.42% state average; 70.58% had 0% treatment), and population sewage service coverage averaged 39.39% across the analyzed BHL population (537,298 residents, 84.54% of BHL; 4 municipalities at 0%). Per capita sewage investment in 2016–2017 was below R$ 0.20 in 10 of 12 analyzed municipalities (at least 50% of the 20 BHL municipalities), with only Ilhéus exceeding the state average in 2017 (R$ 42.63 per inhabitant). Regarding legal/governance mechanisms, 10 years after Law 11.445/2007 only 15% (3/20) of municipalities had completed a Municipal Basic Sanitation Plan (PMSB) by 2017, 40% (8/20) were drafting one, and 45% (9/20) had none, leaving 85% (17/20) ineligible for federal sanitation transfers starting in 2020 under Decree 9.254/2017. Only 35% (7/20) had complete 2016–2017 sewage data in SNIS; among the 13 municipalities sent Freedom of Information (LAI) requests, 69.23% (9/13) had an agency linked in e-SIC (4 required physical filing due to unlinked portals and 1 restricted online filing via a closed profession list), and 4–5 failed to respond within the statutory 20-day (+10-day) deadline.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 17–27, Section 3, Figures 1–4, Tables 1–3, and Quadro 1; PDF p. 28–29, Section 4

mechanism_certainty.comment: Ceiling is 2 under Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework. Coded as 1 because while the authors directly audit municipal PMSB status and e-SIC/LAI administrative barriers to researcher data requests, the relationship between these legal/governance mechanisms and actual household sanitation access/coverage in 2016–2017 is documented only through parallel descriptive municipal indicators (and the federal budget transfer cutoff for lacking a PMSB under Decree 9.254/2017 was prospective for 2020 rather than directly observed operating on 2016–2017 sanitation access).
